content:
You are a domain driven design (DDD) expert.
Your task is to help the user step by step with creating domain models.

### Here is the explanation of the workflow:
1. The user will provide domain information.
2. Next You will carry out the modeling steps, but only once the user specifically requests it.

#### Modeling steps:
1. You will extract domain objects and associations. 
2. You will group the objects by subdomains.
3. In the last step you will define bounded contexts.

Help me extract domain objects. Below I will provide domain information. 

#### Data:
This domain information covers the important domain events:
```json
{
  "domain-information": [
    "As a camp administrator, I want to register campers and parents so that I can manage enrollments efficiently.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to update and remove camper information so that records stay accurate.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to schedule activities and assign staff so that the camp runs smoothly.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to track which campers submitted forms so that all legal requirements are met.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to store emergency and medical information so that I can act quickly in case of incidents.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to send notifications to all parents so that they stay informed about events.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to create and manage camp rules so that everyone understands expected behavior.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to organize campers into groups so that activities are better coordinated.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to monitor the use of camp facilities so that schedules do not conflict.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to collect and review parent feedback so that I can improve camp services.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to view and modify the staff list and their assigned roles so that responsibilities are clear.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to maintain records from previous years so that setup for the next camp is easier.",
    "As a parent, I want to create an account and enroll my children so that they can join the camp.",
    "As a parent, I want to view my childâ€™s schedule and activities so that I know what they are doing.",
    "As a parent, I want to sign and submit consent forms online so that registration is easier.",
    "As a parent, I want to message counselors so that I can ask about my childâ€™s progress.",
    "As a parent, I want to see which counselors are responsible for my child so that I know who to contact.",
    "As a parent, I want to confirm my payments so that I know I have met all financial obligations.",
    "As a parent, I want to connect with camp staff in case of an emergency so that I can get quick updates.",
    "As a camp worker, I want to see the list of campers I supervise so that I can manage them properly.",
    "As a camp worker, I want to report supplies or repairs needed so that the camp stays functional.",
    "As a camp worker, I want to report misbehavior so that administrators can take appropriate action.",
    "As a camp counselor, I want to take attendance of my assigned campers so that I can ensure everyone is present.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to generate nametags automatically so that setup is faster.",
    "As a camp administrator, I want to set reminders for important tasks so that I donâ€™t miss deadlines."
  ]
}
```

#### Task:
- Identify the objects within this information. 
- Summarize it's meaning in a short description. 
- If you can make out attributes that are essential to the object, add them too. 
- Return the objects in json format. Here is an example for structuring the data:
```json
{
  "domain objects": [
    {
      "name": "...",
      "description": "..."
    }
  ]
}
```

Help me find the associations. Below I will provide the current state of the domain. 

#### Data:
These are the domain objects we extracted so far:
```json

```

#### Task:
- Draw connections between objects that have an association. 
- Name each object and add a description that captures the meaning of the association.
- Return the associations in json format. Here is an example for structuring the data:
```json
{
  "associations": [
    {
      "from": "...",
      "to": "...",
      "description": "..."
    }
  ]
}
```

Here are the bounded contexts: 
```json
{
  "bounded contexts": {
    "Camping": {
      "derived from": "Camping Subdomain",
      "objects": [
        "Camp",
        "Activity",
        "Staff",
        "Camp Rules",
        "Camp Facility",
        "Camp Schedule",
        "Camper Group",
        "Camp Worker"
      ],
      "name changes": [
        "Camp Worker -> Camp Worker"
      ]
    },
    "Enrollment": {
      "derived from": "Enrollment Subdomain",
      "objects": [
        "Enrollment",
        "Parent",
        "Camper Records",
        "Emergency Information",
        "Medical Information",
        "Camper"
      ],
      "name changes": [
        "Camper Records -> Submission Camper Records",
        "Parent -> Parent"
      ]
    },
    "Parenting": {
      "derived from": "Parenting Subdomain",
      "objects": [
        "Parent",
        "Child",
        "Child Schedule",
        "Counselor",
        "Parent Feedback Post"
      ],
      "name changes": [
        "Parent -> Camper Parent",
        "Parent Feedback -> Parent Feedback Post",
        "Camper -> Child",
        "Schedule -> Child Schedule"
      ]
    },
    "Administration": {
      "derived from": "Administration Subdomain",
      "objects": [
        "Camp Administrator",
        "Parent Feedback Report",
        "Camper Records",
        "Emergency Information",
        "Medical Information",
        "Camp Worker",
        "Worker Report"
      ],
      "name changes": [
        "Camp Worker -> Reporting Camp Worker",
        "Camper Records -> Camper Records",
        "Parent Feedback -> Parent Feedback Report",
        "Report -> Worker Report"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
